LIFE · 01—02

Instructions for one life

01

Watch your world grow.

Begin at birth. Family comes first; the neighbourhood appears as you grow.

02

Divide ten points.

At 10, choose your starting attributes. Every five years, decide where to put your effort.

01
03

Read the turns.

Follow health, wellbeing and money. Event markers explain changes; they do not predict your future.

04

Look back.

When a life ends, compare your intentions with the path you lived. Try another path in the same world.

Time controls

Ⅱ　2×　3×　10×　20×

Pause to look. Use 2×, 3×, 10× or 20× to move faster.

No choices before 10. No life has a guaranteed length.

Research

What is measured?

This prototype uses authored game rules. Its money, health changes and event odds are not measured population statistics.

The graphs join five-year snapshots. Markers sit at the recorded review age, not an exact event date.

Ten points are a game constraint. Reasoning, empathy and strength are not biological opposites.

The neighbourhood is metaphorical. Nearby buildings represent parts of a life, not a real map.

Dengue, job loss, marriage and pregnancy have marker designs, but are not yet generated by this model. No invented milestones are added to your saved life.
